title: Dedicated capacity: partitioned-burst & graceful-failover patterns PRD
creator: Leah Kim
description: This PRD defines a set of features and operational patterns that enable: (1) partitioned burst policies that allow tenants to use short-lived extra capacity in bounded partitions without jeopardizing other tenants, and (2) graceful failover/fallback behaviors when a tenants reserved pool is depleted or a cell experiences localized degradation. The goal is to provide predictable tenant QoS, clear preemption semantics, and observable signals for operators and customers.
background: Customer and internal incidents over the last 12 months show two recurring problems in Dedicated: noisy bursts that cause neighbor latency spikes, and brittle fallback behavior when reserved pools are exhausted (sudden 503s, heavy throttling, or silent queuing). Existing reserve + burst models are single-contour and rely on coarse preemption which often leads to user-visible disruption. We need a safer containment model and an operator-friendly failover surface that preserves latency SLOs for high-priority tenants while allowing opportunistic borrowing by lower-priority workloads.
goals: Define partition semantics: partitions within a tenants allocation to bound burst impact and enforce per-partition preemption rules
Provide an automatic, latency-aware failover path from reserved pool -> shared backfill -> best-effort pool with controlled degradation
Expose telemetry and alerts for preemption events, failovers, and partition saturation to Console and ops playbooks
Design API/config primitives for customers to opt into partitioned burst policies and declare priority classes/credit budgets
non_goals: Replacing or redesigning the global autoscaler algorithm (only integration hooks required)
Implementing hardware-level kernel changes or custom low-level model runtime optimizations
Providing fine-grained per-request QoS tokens for arbitrary hosted workloads (out of scope for this phase)
requirements: R1: Partitioned burst contract - tenants can request N logical partitions per reservation with configurable max-burst-duration and max-tokens-per-second per partition
R2: Preemption policy - define deterministic eviction order: partition-level oldest-first within same priority, priority-class preemption between classes

R3: Failover choreography - when a tenants reserved pool is saturated or node-local capacity is degraded, requests are routed to fallback pools according to latency-cost policies and per-tenant allowed fallbacks
R4: Observable events - preemption, partition-saturation, failover-triggered, fallback-completed events emitted with request hashes and sample telemetry
R5: Console UI - new Dedicated > Capacity > Partitions view showing partition health, active borrow, recent preemptions, and a way to adjust partition sizing and priority classes
R6: API - Extend Reserve API to accept partition schema and priority classes; make explicit the expected SLO degradation ranges when opting into fallback
R7: Safety knobs - emergency cutoff, grace-period timers, and soft-eviction thresholds configurable by operators and exposed as defaults to customers
R8: Test harness - synthetic workload + chaos tests that validate failover correctness across node, zone, and pool failures
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Partition creation flow works end-to-end from API -> control plane -> compute nodes; partitions enforced for CPU/GPU token budgets and token accounting matches expectations in 95th percentile tests
AC2: Preemption sequence reproducible in staging: lower-priority partition traffic gets evicted before higher-priority partitions with no request-level inconsistencies observed in 1000-sample runs
AC3: Failover path completes within target SLOs: cold-fallback (shared backfill) median additional latency <= 120ms, and worst-case tail within defined degradation budget for the tenant
AC4: Console surfaces partition health and last 72 hours of preemption/failover events with links to trace IDs and sample payloads
AC5: Telemetry events are emitted to observability pipelines (Tracing/Logs/Metric) and trigger alerts in runbook scenarios documented in the ops playbook
AC6: Chaos experiments (node drain, zone loss) produce graceful degradation instead of systemic queue growth or OOMs in 95% of runs
AC7: API schema documented and SDKs for Python/Go/Node include examples and error codes for partition/fallback conditions
success_metrics: SM1: Reduction in customer-impacting 5xx events caused by reserve exhaustion by >= 80% for tenants who opt into partitioned burst
SM2: Neighbor latency spike frequency (p99 token latency across tenants in same cell) reduced by >= 60% during bursts
SM3: Mean time to detect and annotate a preemption or failover event in Console <= 2 minutes
SM4: Adoption: at least 30% of new Dedicated reservations created in the quarter opt into partitioned-burst policy
SM5: Post-launch ops load: fewer than 1 paging incident per week attributable to reserved pool overflow for 90+ days
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design & API): finalize partition model, preemption semantics, API contracts, and console mockups - 3 weeks
Phase 1 (Runtime & Control Plane): implement partition enforcement, token accounting, and deterministic preemption hooks - 4 weeks
Phase 2 (Observability & UI): wire telemetry events to Console, add partition dashboards and runbook links - 2 weeks
Phase 3 (Staging + Chaos): run synthetic and chaos tests across cells, tune failover thresholds, and document runbooks - 3 weeks
Phase 4 (Canary): opt-in pilot with 3 low-risk customers; monitor metrics and rollback criteria - 2 weeks
Phase 5 (Gradual ramp): expand to all new reservations and provide migration guidance for existing customers - 6 weeks
risks: R1: Incorrect token accounting could allow tenants to exceed compute budgets; mitigation: cross-validate with billing signals and add hard caps
R2: Excessive preemption churn could increase tail latency; mitigation: add cooldown windows and leader-elected eviction batching
R3: Customers may misunderstand expected degradation during fallback; mitigation: explicit API flags and in-Console warnings with example latency curves
R4: Telemetry volume increase from preemption/failover events may push observability costs; mitigation: sampling + aggregated counters
